message.content: {"thought": "The FFN1 tilings all have identical latency_sum (2.84s) and latency_max (2.82s), and all share the same critical_end (10.55s), meaning they execute in parallel across cores. Each tiling is purely compute-bound with negligible NoC/DRAM time. The 32 FFN1 tilings collectively contribute 32 * 2.84s = 90.9B of compute time, but the total timeline is only 10.58s, confirming they run in parallel across the 32 chiplets. The 45.5% average utilization and 1.6x imbalance suggest some chiplets are idle while others compute FFN1 tilings. I need to understand the scheduling: are all 32 FFN1 tilings mapped to different cores, or are they serialized? The critical_end being identical suggests parallel execution. The imbalance likely comes from the FFN2 and attention layers that follow. To complete the diagnosis, I should check the operator group summary to see the full picture of FFN vs attention vs other groups, and then I can finalize the bottleneck state.", "action": "tool", "tool": {"name": "summarize_operator_groups", "arguments": {"sort_by": "latency_sum", "top_groups": 5, "include_components": true}}}
